page: Google Cloud Platform g1-small is a shared-core virtual machine instance designed for entry-level workloads. It features 1 vCPU allocated from a shared physical Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 2.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.7 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of compute and memory capabilities. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both yield a score of 1076.89, reflecting the shared nature of the single physical core. Memory bandwidth is limited, with uncached read speeds at 10.49 GB/sec and write speeds at 8.91 GB/sec. Database operations under Passmark score 564.91, while Redis SET operations achieve 0.59 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput is measured at 0.54 GB/sec.

Given its shared-core architecture and low resource density, the g1-small offers a highly cost-efficient profile for non-demanding, intermittent tasks. It is best suited for lightweight applications, basic web serving, development environments, and small-scale testing where continuous high CPU utilization is not required.
